quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on your driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan your travel time realistically, follow the speed limit, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready for unexpected conditions.
Expect construction workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for unexpected conditions.
questions.explanation: Construction zones can have unexpected hazards. Drive slowly and carefully to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: What do defensive drivers do?

options.text: Trust that other drivers will do the right thing.
Think about what other drivers might do and prepare to respond.
Drive aggressively and never let other drivers pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Think about what other drivers might do and prepare to respond.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means predicting possible mistakes by other drivers and being ready to react to them.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?

options.text: Side mirrors eliminate all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than cars.
You can see blind spots using your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots, so other vehicles should avoid these areas.

questions.question: What should you do before passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Honk your horn while you pass.
Flash your headlights while you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is difficult to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. Always make sure you have enough space to change lanes safely when passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near people who are blind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near people who are blind.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It can startle or confuse them. Yield to the pedestrian and continue driving when it is safe.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Only look in the left outside mirror.
Look over your shoulder.
Only look in the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If the fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When you are behind a small car.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly, as this can cause a collision.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it can help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it can help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when it is necessary to avoid a crash. Do not use your horn just because a driver is moving slowly or you want them to get out of your way.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you can go in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait for the light to change.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. Before turning, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns you about possible danger ahead. Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of possible dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Let other traffic and pedestrians go first. Then proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks if you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass, but only if it is safe.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn on:

options.text: The dashboard lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers cannot see you. Always use your low beam headlights when you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn can be made here.
A left turn can be made only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn can be made here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road surface, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before trying to stop or turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions right ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
Only the right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange warning signs or equipment on the road.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is risky. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take dangerous chances to pass you.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must let the pedestrians cross first.
You have the right to go before the pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let the pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: When you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection. Drivers must always let pedestrians cross when turning on a green light.

questions.question: A school bus in front of you has red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: It is very foggy. You should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and dust, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red flashing lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm folds back.
The stop arm folds back and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm folds back and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights and the stop arm out, stay stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm folds back, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Usually only affect large vehicles.
Only cause problems seeing the road.
Can affect all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, though it creates extra problems for large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility and sometimes physically move any vehicle.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic light colors from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights are always arranged from top to bottom as red, yellow, and green. This is the standard order for all traffic signals.
